manifest.name: dsh-report-fix
manifest.description: DSH guard plugin: a session whose turn was started by session_call(task_dispatch) cannot close its turn until it has sent a task_report back to the caller.
manifest.author: JohnnnSinaaa

scripts.lint: node --check index.mjs && node --check lib/transport.mjs && node --check lib/texts.mjs && node --check lib/guard.mjs && node --check lib/config.mjs && node --check lib/messages.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-report-fix bundle patch: mounts the task_report guard into a DSH profile.
#
# The plugin listens to three host hooks and never registers tools of its own:
#   agent/pre-step      — notices an inbound session_call(task_dispatch) and
#                         (optionally) appends a per-turn reminder message.
#   tools/post-execute  — records a successful session_call(task_report).
#   agent/turn-stopping — the turn is about to close; a missing report is
#                         answered with agent.steer(), which re-opens the turn.
#
# Installed with `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <spec>`, DSH registers this
# bundle in `dsh.profile.bundles` and loads this patch automatically.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-report-fix
      name: dsh-report-fix
      config:
        enabled: true
        # Hard gate: how many times a turn that still owes a task_report may be
        # re-opened before the guard gives up and lets the turn close (0 disables
        # the gate and keeps only the pre-step reminder).
        maxNudges: 3
        # Append a short instruction message right after an inbound task_dispatch
        # so the model knows the contract from the first step of the turn.
        preStepReminder: true
        # 'auto' follows the dispatch message's own language (CJK → zh, else en).
        locale: auto
        # Characters of the original dispatch kept in the blocking message.
        excerptMaxChars: 600

readme.text:
[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README_ZH.md)

[](https://github.com/JohnnnSinaaa/dsh-report-fix/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)
[](https://nodejs.org)

A DSH plugin: **a session whose turn was started by `session_call(task_dispatch)` cannot
close that turn until it has sent a `task_report` back to the caller.**

It adds no tools and changes nothing inside `dsh-call-session`. It listens to three lifecycle
hooks the DSH host already emits, checks the receipt at the turn boundary, and — when the
receipt is missing — injects a fresh instruction message that re-opens the turn, forcing the
model to call `session_call(call_type="task_report")`.

```
session A ──session_call(task_dispatch)──▶ session B
                                            │
                                            ├─ ok:      session_call(task_report) ──▶ A gets the result
                                            └─ missing: final answer, turn closes ───▶ A waits forever

`session_call` is delivery-only: a `task_dispatch` waits at most 300 ms for the handshake and
can never learn whether the callee reported back. This plugin closes that hole — a
dispatch-driven turn can only end in a "reported" state.

| Hook | When | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent/pre-step` | before each step's messages reach the model | recognize inbound `task_dispatch`, register the debt, append a reminder (optional) |
| `tools/post-execute` | after every tool call | a successful `session_call(task_report)` clears the matching debt |
| `agent/turn-stopping` | the turn is about to close (final answer already produced) | if a debt remains, `agent.steer(message)`; the loop re-reads its inbox and runs another step instead of closing |

`agent/turn-stopping` is the only supported way to keep a turn open. The type comment in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent` says it plainly: *Awaited before the boundary commits — a listener
that objects steers (agent.steer(...)) and the machine re-reads its inbox: fresh steering runs
another step, none closes the turn.* This plugin uses exactly that path.

readme.section: How a turn is recognized as dispatch-driven
readme.text:
Every `session_call` delivery is a native user message with `source.kind = 'plugin:dsh-call-session'`
and a transport header on its first line:

```
[From: <callerSessionId> (<callerTitle>) | CallType: task_dispatch]
> Context Ref: #post-...        ← optional

<body>

readme.section: How a turn is recognized as dispatch-driven
readme.text:
The turn counts as dispatch-driven when: `source.kind === 'plugin:dsh-call-session'`,
`source.form === 'notice'` (i.e. delivered by `session_call`, not by `session_create`), the
header parses, and `CallType` is `task_dispatch`. Inbound `notice` / `task_report` messages
create no obligation.

All of the following, in `tools/post-execute`:

- `exec.name === 'session_call'`
- `result.isError !== true` and `result.value.success === true`
- `result.value.callType === 'task_report'`
- `result.value.targetSessionId` matches the caller (case-insensitive; a unique prefix is
  accepted because `session_call` itself supports prefix addressing)

```
[task_report guard · interception 1/3] This turn cannot end: you have not sent a task_report back to the task_dispatch caller.

Awaiting a report (1):
1. 「Worker A」 caller-session-0001

Guard messages follow the inbound message's language (Chinese body → Chinese wording, otherwise
English); `locale` overrides.

1. **The final text has already been produced and may already be visible.** `assistant/message`
   is committed and streamed *before* `agent/turn-stopping` runs, so the guarantee is
   "**the turn does not end without a report**", not "the user never sees the unreported text".
   The latter would need a host hook before finalize; the current DSH version has none.
2. **Bounded interception.** When `maxNudges` (default 3) is spent, the turn is released and a
   `warn` is logged, so a model stuck in a loop cannot pin the turn forever. `maxNudges: 0`
   keeps only the reminder and disables the hard gate.
3. **Obligations are per turn.** A new turn starts clean; a debt is never carried over.
4. **Only successful `task_report`s count.** A tool error, `success: false`, or a report sent to
   the wrong session does not clear the debt.
5. **It follows `dsh-call-session`'s message format.** It imports none of that package and only
   reads `source.kind` / `source.form` / the first-line header, so a format change upstream
   needs a matching update here.
6. Multiple callers in the same turn each get their own debt and must each be reported to.
7. **Conflicting dispatch bodies are decided by t

Override by id in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`dsh-hmr` recomposes the profile, no restart
needed for config):

```yaml
- id: dsh-report-fix
  config:
    maxNudges: 5
    locale: zh

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | master switch; `false` registers no hooks at all |
| `maxNudges` | `3` | interceptions per turn; `0` disables the hard gate and keeps the reminder |
| `preStepReminder` | `true` | append a reminder on the first step, so most turns comply before the gate |
| `locale` | `auto` | `auto` follows the inbound message language; `zh` / `en` force it |
| `excerptMaxChars` | `600` | max characters of the original dispatch quoted in the nudge |

This is a DSH profile plugin (bundle shape): `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and
`cordis.patch.yml` mounts the row with `- insert:`.

readme.section: local checkout (writes into the profile's dependencies and dsh.profile.bundles)
readme.text:
git clone https://github.com/JohnnnSinaaa/dsh-report-fix.git
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/dsh-report-fix"

dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-report-fix
```

After `dsh plugin add`:

- `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` gains `dsh-report-fix` in `dsh.profile.bundles`;bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-report-fix
```

```bash
npm test        # node --test, 40 cases: parsing, state machine, hook wiring
npm run lint    # node --check on every entry and lib module
```

Layout:

```
index.mjs          apply(): wires the three hooks, logging, disposal
lib/transport.mjs  session_call header parsing / session id matching / locale probing
lib/guard.mjs      TurnReportGuard: per agent × turn debts and interception budget
lib/texts.mjs      Chinese / English reminder and nudge wording

The tests replay the host's waterfall / serial semantics with a fake `Agent` and a fake Cordis
`ctx`, covering: user turns untouched, `task_dispatch` registration and interception, report
release, wrong-target and failed reports, `notice` / `task_report` / `session_create` creating no
obligation, duplicate messages counted once, budget exhaustion, per-turn reset, multiple callers,
locale selection, and excerpt truncation.
Three deliveries against a real model on DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` + the web profile (caller → callee):

| Inbound | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `session_create` | first turn has `source.form = session_create`, no obligation, zero guard messages in the log |
| `task_dispatch` "reply with one sentence, do not report back" | reminder injected on the first step; after the final answer the callee was intercepted three times (`1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3`), each interception followed by another step (turn stayed open); `turn/end` only after the budget was spent |
| `task_dispatch` "report first, then answer" | the model called `session_call(task_report)`, the caller received it, no interception in that turn, `turn/end` with `reason.kind = completed` |

The caller's own (user-initiated) turn received the `task_report` with zero guard messages,
confirming the guard only books `task_dispatch`.

Session logs can be replayed with
`zstdcat ~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace>/<session-id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`: guard messages appear
as `user/message` events with `source.kind = dsh-report-fix`.

- DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`
- Depends on the profile plugin `dsh-call-session` (message format only, no version pin)
- Node `>=20`, zero runtime dependencies
